description: Intelligent Driver Model with AR(5) noise on velocity-prediction residuals (IDM+AR). Adapted from the published Bayesian dynamic-regression framework — Chengyuan Zhang, Wenshuo Wang, Lijun Sun, 'Calibrating Car-following Models via Bayesian Dynamic Regression' (arXiv 2307.03340).
assumptions: Pooled population IDM parameters. Acceleration clipped to [-10, 5] m/s^2. Forward velocity: v_{t+1} = max(v_t + a_IDM(v_t, dv_t, s_t)*dt + eps_t, 0). AR(5) innovation: eps_t = sum_{k=1..5} rho_k * eps_{t-k} + eta_t, eta_t ~ N(0, sigma_eta^2). At test time the AR chain is warm-started from the 5 most recent observed residuals computed on the 2.9 s of history.
calibration: Two-stage calibration on OpenCF train.csv (Waymo, dt=0.1, urban: q99 follower_speed = 19.6 m/s). Stage 1 (IDM): differential-evolution closed-loop velocity-RMSE fit over 30-step (3.0 s) rollouts on 4,000 random pairs, urban-typical bounds. Result: v0=28.46, T=0.99, a=1.31, b=0.54, s0=3.29 (delta=4 fixed). Stage 2 (AR(5) coefficients): Yule-Walker estimate on IDM residuals from 2,000 pairs (177,988 transitions). Result: rho = [1.022, -0.145, 0.167, -0.038, -0.057] (stationarity-checked: max reciprocal-root modulus < 0.95), sigma_eta = 0.0344 m/s. PyMC NUTS pooled joint inference (800 pairs, prior-scale=0.3 anchored at the DE point) was also explored but the one-step-prediction likelihood pulls IDM away from the closed-loop optimum — the DE-anchored two-stage fit was retained. At inference, 6 trajectories per pair are simulated with the calibrated IDM, the AR(5) chain is warm-started from each pair's last 5 observed residuals (computed against the calibrated IDM), and innovations eta_t are drawn independently per sample.
